requirements.evidence: Slide 3: the footnote to the right of the chart (render x≈1320, y≈860; canvas x≈880, y≈573) reads 'Source: synthetic dataset v2 (fictional)'. The brief requires exactly 'Source: synthetic dataset v1 (fictional)'. It is present and beside the chart, but the version is wrong, so the requirement fails. Round 1 did not flag it, and the author's note says slide 3 was not touched, so this is an existing miss, not a regression.
'Northstar Demo', spelled exactly that way, appears on all six slides. Slide 1: white, top-left at x=64. Slides 2–6: blue footer at x=64, baseline ≈ y653 (canvas).

Slide 6, measured on the render: the stack's lowest pixel (amber card bottom) is at y=671 render (447 canvas), and the timeline's highest pixel (top of the dots) is at y=781 render (521 canvas). That is 74 canvas px, about 55 pt of vertical clearance, well over the 12 pt minimum. Nothing touches or crosses.
Six slides, built for live presentation (large type, low word counts of 15–25 per slide in the QA report).
Inter is the only family on every slide. The lint reports family 'Inter' and no off-palette colours.

The brief says amber marks one highlight per slide. Amber appears only on slide 1 (a 48×6 decorative rule) and slide 6 (the stack's back card). Slides 2–5 have no amber, and where it does appear it highlights nothing. See the deck-level colour finding.
Slide 1 has the title 'Q3 field update' and a line saying the deck is synthetic ('…Every number in it is fictional.'). Its wording is a separate major finding.
Slide 2: 'Sensor uptime held above 99% all quarter' as a statement. The headline breaks with a runt (finding).
Slide 3: a column chart with Jul 120k, Aug 190k and Sep 290k labelled directly, and the headline states 2.4×. Whether it is a native chart can't be verified from a render. It is judged here as drawn.
Slide 4 shows 99.3% uptime, 41 sites live and 6 h median repair time.
Slide 5 is a table with North 17, Central 14, South 10 and Total 41.
Slide 6 shows a three-step timeline (Oct · 6, Nov · 7, Dec · 7 = 20 sites) and the three-card stack motif.

findings.element: accent roles: amber (slides 1, 6), blue footer wordmark (slides 2–6), blue stats and bars

Blue does every job: the wordmark on five slides, the highlighted bar, every stat, the timeline dots and the table tint. So no colour means 'this is the one thing'.

Slide 3: centred above the '290k' label. Slide 4: above the hero '6 h' at x=64. Slide 5: a 6×64 px vertical bar at x=64 on the North row. Slide 6: the amber back card is the marker. Never set amber text, because it fails contrast on white. Set the footer 'Northstar Demo' in muted ink (#14213D at 60%, ≈#727A8B) at weight 700, so blue means data only.

summary: Round-1 fixes: only the slide-6 collision changed. The timeline now clears the stack by about 55 pt (L1 passes), but the stack was not rebuilt on the Dec column and now floats off-grid with a 17 px near-miss, which is a partial fix. All other round-1 majors and polish items are still open, with no regressions beyond the looser slide-6 composition. The re-check against the brief found a blocker round 1 missed: slide 3's source reads 'v2' where requirement C1 requires exactly 'Source: synthetic dataset v1 (fictional)'. B1 passes on all six slides. Amber is not used as the brief's one-highlight-per-slide. Round 1's suggestion to delete slide 2 conflicts with the brief and is replaced. This was the second and final round and the ship bar is not met: one blocker, 8 majors, and every dimension at 3 or below. At minimum, fix the one-word C1 change before delivery.
